metadata.title: EDI and B2B Document Exchange Platform Residuality Stress Test
metadata.description: How the Transus platform must change when e-invoicing law, security regulation, AI, group ownership, retailer choices or infrastructure failures shift.
metadata.naiveArchitecture: Point-to-point mappings hand-built per customer and retailer, one transport server, invoices as a special case outside EDI, portal and support tools reading the same database, security answers written per questionnaire.
metadata.residualArchitecture: A network registry and retailer profile library feeding one translation and validation engine; e-invoice formats as profiles; AI-proposed mappings with human review; durable queues and a replicated status ledger; one public API used by ERPs, partners and Katapull siblings alike; assurance as a maintained artefact.
metadata.note: Stressors are reasoned from public Transus and Katapull sources; status values are the author's assessment, not Transus statements.

stressors.name: Germany makes sending e-invoices mandatory (2027-2028)
stressors.detection: Customers with German buyers ask for XRechnung/ZUGFeRD; published dates 1 January 2027 (turnover above EUR 800,000) and 1 January 2028 (all).
stressors.attractor: Every supplier trading with Germany needs structured invoices; PDF invoicing stops working.
stressors.businessReaction: Support EN 16931 formats and Peppol via Tickstar inside the existing EDI flow; validate before sending.
stressors.residue: E-invoice formats are profiles in the same translation and validation engine; country mandates become configuration.

impacts.effect: Builds EN 16931 formats and Peppol transmission.
Mandate coverage becomes the key metric.

stressors.name: Customers under NIS2 audit their EDI supplier
stressors.detection: Security questionnaires referencing the Dutch Cybersecurity Act; requests for faster incident reporting.
stressors.attractor: Enterprise customers buy only from suppliers proving security, continuity and incident handling.
stressors.businessReaction: Publish an ISO 27001:2022-backed NIS2 information pack; allow contractual incident-reporting arrangements.
stressors.residue: Assurance evidence is a maintained product artefact, not ad hoc answers.

impacts.effect: Holds controls and the assurance pack.

stressors.name: AI makes partner mapping a commodity
stressors.detection: Competitors and ERP vendors advertise AI-generated EDI mappings; prospects question onboarding fees.
stressors.attractor: Speed of connection stops differentiating; value shifts to network reach, monitoring and trust.
stressors.businessReaction: Ship Traci AI, keep specialists for review, and invest in monitoring and partner data quality.
stressors.residue: Mappings are generated from profiles plus samples and reviewed; the profile library and network remain the asset.

impacts.effect: Scale competitor with own AI investments.

stressors.name: Katapull expects Transus to serve the whole Commerce Hub
stressors.detection: Interim management from Katapull (2026); sibling brands listed as Transus partners; group cross-selling targets.
stressors.attractor: Pressure to productise connectors for Logic4, Vendit, Highbiza, EffectConnect, DeliveryMatch, Returnista and Picqer while keeping open ERP neutrality.
stressors.businessReaction: Build a Commerce Hub connector layer on the same public API used by external partners.
stressors.residue: Sibling links are ordinary API clients; no special-case integrations inside the core.

media.alt: Illustration of the residuality stressor 'Katapull expects Transus to serve the whole Commerce Hub', showing its signal, attractor, business response, and surviving residue.

stressors.name: A major retailer moves its suppliers to a competing network
stressors.detection: Retailer announces a preferred EDI provider or supplier portal; suppliers ask about migration.
stressors.attractor: Suppliers may be pushed to a competitor for that retailer and consolidate there.
stressors.businessReaction: Interconnect with other networks so suppliers keep one provider; emphasise multi-retailer value.
stressors.residue: Network interconnects are a first-class transport route, so no single retailer decides the supplier's provider.

impacts.effect: Protects fulfilment quality during the switch.

media.title: Residuality stressor illustration: A major retailer moves its suppliers to a competing network
media.alt: Illustration of the residuality stressor 'A major retailer moves its suppliers to a competing network', showing its signal, attractor, business response, and surviving residue.

stressors.name: Primary data centre outage during peak ordering
stressors.detection: Monitoring shows the Frankfurt site unavailable; partners report undelivered orders.
stressors.attractor: Orders and despatch advice stall across thousands of trading relationships within hours.
stressors.businessReaction: Fail over to the Amsterdam disaster-recovery site and replay queued messages; inform customers through the incident procedure.
stressors.residue: Durable queues and replicated status ledgers let delivery resume without loss or duplicates.
